content:
Stephanie Nguyen: Hey folks — we’re getting a bunch of Dedicated questions again and the answers are drifting 😅

Can we get a sales-friendly cheat sheet for the new Dedicated throughput tiers?
- what each tier *means* in plain English
- qualifying questions
- what we can/can’t promise (esp tokens/sec)
- and guidance for exception asks ("can you guarantee 2x?", "we need H100 in eu-central")

Even a draft one-pager would help for next week.

Jordan Blake: +1. Also need something we can copy/paste into emails. Right now every AE is improvising.

Lukas Meyer: +1 from EMEA — region availability is the biggest landmine. Prospects keep asking for Premium in EU regions where supply is tight.

Lauren Bishop: Yep, agreed. We’re finalizing the tier spec + measurement standard, but we can absolutely get a one-pager out ahead of full Confluence publishing.

What I can share today:
- Tier names are still: Standard / Performance / Premium (unless we get strong pushback)
- Primary guarantee is throughput measured as *sustained output tokens/sec over a defined window* (not "req/sec") with explicit assumptions/exclusions
- We will have a clear "what happens under overload" section (expected throttling vs SLO breach)

I’ll pull together a v0 cheat sheet and post here.

Stephanie Nguyen: Amazing. Timing-wise, can we get it by EOD tomorrow? Enablement session is Tuesday.

Lauren Bishop: I can do EOD tomorrow for v0 (good enough to use on calls). Polished v1 early next week after SRE/Legal final pass.

Talia Benson: Jumping in — I’ll track this as a deliverable for the rollout plan. Lauren, I’ll DM you the template we used for last quarter’s packaging one-pager.

Jordan Blake: For exceptions, can we define a simple rule like: "anything above published tier guarantees = exception" and then we route through a single approval path?

Lauren Bishop: Yes. Proposed policy (draft):
1) If customer asks for guarantees outside published tier thresholds, shape, or region availability → exception.
2) Exceptions require: Product (me) + Infra (Irene/Vanessa) feasibility + Finance (Laura/Rishi) pricing uplift + Legal (Michael/Sofia Mendes) if language changes.
3) We do *not* commit on calls. We say: "We can evaluate an exception based on workload + region + term; we’ll come back with a written addendum if approved."

I’ll add exact suggested wording to the cheat sheet.

Lukas Meyer: Can we have a crisp answer for "can you guarantee 10k tokens/sec"? That’s the line we get constantly.

Lauren Bishop: Yes, but it needs to be framed correctly:
- We guarantee at the *deployment* level under a baseline workload profile, and it’s model + context-length dependent.
- We should not quote a raw number without asking: model, avg input tokens, avg output tokens, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming.

Cheat-sheet will include a quick checklist + the safe response:
"We can guarantee throughput under documented assumptions; if you share your workload profile we can map you to the right tier/shape and confirm in writing."

Laura Bennett: +1. Please make it obvious when quoting numbers triggers pricing review. If we’re doing more than the published tier, we need an uplift or we’ll blow margin.

Jordan Blake: Also need a rule for "we need H100s" (or A100 80GB) when they’re not generally available.

Lauren Bishop: We’ll include a hard "availability constraints" box:
- Premium = limited regions / subject to supply
- Some shapes only in specific regions
- If they need a locked region + specific GPU, that’s either: a) longer lead time, b) different tier, or c) exception.

Michael Grant: Legal note: please avoid the word "guarantee" in email copy until the official SLA clause is in the order form / MSA addendum. Use "throughput commitment" or "SLO" and reference the measurement standard.

Stephanie Nguyen: Good call. Can we bake that into the copy/paste language?

Lauren Bishop: Yep.

Draft structure I’ll send tomorrow:
- What is Dedicated throughput SLO (one paragraph)
- Tier summary table (Standard/Performance/Premium): what’s included, burst policy, customer reporting
- Qualification questions (workload + region + model)
- What to say / not say (approved phrases)
- Exceptions: when required + how to request + expected turnaround

Talia Benson: What’s the turnaround we want to commit to on exception requests?

Lauren Bishop: Draft:
- Simple shape/region exceptions: 2–3 business days (assuming no legal language change)
- Anything that changes contract language: 1–2 weeks depending on redlines

We can refine after we see first few requests.

Jordan Blake: Works. Please also include "common objections" → "we can’t risk throttling" / "we need true burst" / "why can’t you just autoscale".

Lauren Bishop: Will do. Overload behavior section is exactly for that.

Stephanie Nguyen: Thank you. Please post the doc link here when ready — we’ll pin it in #sales.

Lauren Bishop: Will post tomorrow.

—

Lauren Bishop (next day): v0 cheat sheet draft is up here (Google Doc): https://drive.google.com/redwood/dedicated-throughput-tiers-cheatsheet-draft

Please comment inline by Monday 12pm PT so we can lock v1 for Tuesday enablement.

Jordan Blake: Looking now. :eyes:

Lukas Meyer: Added comments on EMEA region phrasing + avoid promising "EU only" if fallback can route. :thumbsup:

Michael Grant: Left 2 comments in the “approved language” section. Main change: replace “credit” wording with “service credits per SLA” and don’t specify amounts until the SLA schedule is finalized.

Laura Bennett: Added note: exception asks should include term + commit, otherwise we shouldn’t even start pricing.

Lauren Bishop: Got it. I’ll incorporate all comments and publish v1 to Confluence early next week + share a PDF version for outbound emails.
